paragraphs: R' Yehudah ben Nekosah. (Tanna). Hyman states that he was among the heads of the generation in the time of Rabbi and received [teaching] from the sages of the generation before Rabbi, as we find that he spoke in the name of Sumkhos (as in Bava Kamma39a), in the name of R' Yaakov (Chullin118b), and in the name of R' Shimon (Tosefta Negaim ch. 4, halakhah 3). Hyman continues that afterwards he sat before Rabbi, as in Bava Batra71a, where he gave an explanation before Rabbi. And in Bava Kamma81b it is related that once Rabbi and R-Ch were walking on the road,

they withdrew to the sides of the roads and saw that R' Yehudah ben Kenosa (Hyman says it should read Nekosa, citing Dikdukei Soferim) was striding along ahead of them. Rabbi said to R-Ch: “Who is this who displays greatness before us?” R-Ch said to him: “Perhaps it is R' Yehudah ben Nekosah, my student (Hyman says it should read ‘your student’, citing Dikdukei Soferim), and all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven.” When they reached him, he said to him: “Were you not Yehudah ben Nekosa, I would have cut your shins with an iron saw.” (And as for

his calling him his student, Hyman explains that it is because he was the Nasi). He is mentioned in a baraita in Yoma18a and in Kohelet Rabbah ch. 1, “פסוק חד” (literal supplied locator, sense uncertain): the heretics would engage with him and question him, and he would answer — his students said to him: “Rabbi, Heaven assisted you and you prevailed.”
